items.title: How Much of a Harness Does a Strong Agent Need for Autonomous ML Engineering?
items.snippet: Recent autonomous machine learning engineering (MLE) agents have made significant progress on public leaderboards. In this paper we find that, under an equal time budget and the same frontier LLM backbone, open-source state-of-the-art harnesses provide no advantages over a single session of a minimal-harness coding agent baseline, pointing to the backbone as the primary driver for performance.

items.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization (SCAPO)
items.snippet: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has improved the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs), yet their predictions remain sensitive to task-irrelevant prompt features. We introduce Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization (SCAPO), a causally inspired variant of GRPO that incorporates semifactual stability into token-level credit assignment. (from 1st tool output)

items.title: Population Fidelity: Evaluating Population Representativeness in LLMs
items.snippet: This article proposes a framework for evaluating population fidelity, which measures how well large language models (LLMs) represent a population's responses. The framework assesses three dimensions: population accuracy, variability, and structure of variability. Findings indicate that cultural fine-tuning improves central alignment but does not enhance the representation of intra-population differences. (from 1st tool output)

items.title: PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent: A self-improving RLM agent for coding workflows and long-running autonomous tasks.
items.snippet: Prime Agent is an open-source coding and research agent for general and long-running work. It is designed around two core abstractions: The Recursive Language Model (RLM) treats context as variables (prompt-as-a-variable) and tools like recursive subagents as function calls (programmatic tool /sub-agent calling) inside a persistent REPL.

items.title: Build agent memory with NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit and Amazon S3 Vectors
items.snippet: The NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit (NAT) offers four capabilities relevant to production agent systems: agent orchestration, profiling, evaluation, and an automatic memory wrapper. This post explores how NAT’s automatic memory wrapper simplifies agent design by abstracting memory management, allowing agents to capture and retrieve conversation history, user preferences, and long-term knowledge without explicit memory tool invocation.

items.title: How Much Is an AI Token Worth? Scaling Laws for Wild AI-Generated Web Text
items.snippet: Web text makes up the majority of pretraining data and is increasingly AI-generated. We pretrain 800 language models, varying the ratio of added AI tokens to human tokens, and fit scaling laws to held-out losses on both human and AI-generated text. Our scaling law predicts the effect of AI text on held-out human-text loss for models up to 3.6x larger with 41% lower error than the best existing law over all AI ratios.

items.title: SoL-Refiner: Speed-of-Light One-Step Refinement for High-Resolution Video
items.snippet: High-resolution video generation is expensive, as its cost grows rapidly with the number of spatiotemporal tokens. We present SoL-Refiner, a one-step video refiner that transforms low-resolution model outputs into 4K videos with a single denoising step. Our three-stage recipe combines high-resolution continual training, reinforcement learning (RL) post-training, and a final one-step distillation.

dropped.snippet: As of October 1st, 2026, arXiv is instituting an updated rate limiting policy across all submitters and categories as a stopgap while we determine what may be the new best practice for authors employing more and more advanced AI tools. arXiv now limits submitters to up to two submissions per calendar month, with a limit of three total active submissions at any given time.
